memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then Jacob said to Laban, 'Give me my wife. My time is completed, and I want to make love to her.' So Laban brought together all the people of the place and gave a feast. But when evening came, he took his daughter Leah and brought her to Jacob, and Jacob made love to her. And Laban gave his servant Zilpah to his daughter as her attendant." - Gen 29:21-24 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
After seven years, the wedding day finally comes. But under the cover of darkness and celebration, Laban carries out a stunning deception — he brings Leah, not Rachel, to Jacob. The veiled bride, the dim light, the wedding feast: Jacob is completely fooled, and does not discover the truth until morning.

It is impossible to miss the irony. Jacob, who had once disguised himself in the dark to deceive his blind father and steal his brother's blessing, is now himself deceived in the dark by a substituted family member. The trickster has been tricked. What he did to his father has, in a sense, been done to him.

This is a striking picture of a sobering truth: "A man reaps what he sows" (Gal 6:7). God had not forgotten Jacob's deception; in His providence, He allowed Jacob to taste the bitterness of being deceived. This was not cruelty but a kind of hard mercy — part of how God was humbling and reshaping Jacob's character over these years.

We should let this search our own hearts. The ways we treat others have a way of coming back to us. But we can also take comfort: when we face the painful harvest of our past, God is often at work in it, shaping us into people who will finally learn to walk in truth.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where might I be sowing something I would not want to reap?
2. Have I ever tasted the very treatment I once gave others?
3. Can I trust that God is shaping me even through painful consequences?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, help me to sow honesty and kindness, for I will reap what I sow. And where I face the harvest of past wrongs, use it to shape me into a person of truth. Amen.
